entries.label: Loopback IP
entries.notes: Baseline probe: reach the loopback interface the server sees but the client cannot.

entries.label: Loopback hostname
entries.notes: Hostname form behaves differently from the raw IP when allowlists or resolvers treat them apart.

entries.label: AWS metadata root
entries.notes: AWS instance metadata service; high-value SSRF target for role credentials.

entries.label: AWS IAM credentials path
entries.notes: Lists IAM role names; read one to retrieve temporary AWS keys.

entries.label: AWS IMDSv2 token endpoint
entries.notes: IMDSv2 needs a PUT with a TTL header; relevant when v1 is disabled.

entries.label: GCP metadata root
entries.notes: GCP metadata; modern setups require the Metadata-Flavor: Google header.

entries.label: Azure IMDS
entries.notes: Azure metadata; requires the Metadata: true header.

entries.label: Decimal-encoded loopback
entries.notes: 127.0.0.1 as a 32-bit decimal integer; bypasses string allowlists of the dotted form.

entries.label: Octal-encoded loopback
entries.notes: Octal first octet; many parsers accept it where filters do not.

entries.label: Hex-encoded loopback
entries.notes: Hex form of 127.0.0.1; another numeric encoding to dodge literal-string blocks.

entries.label: IPv6 loopback
entries.notes: IPv6 loopback bypasses IPv4-only allowlists.

entries.label: IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback
entries.notes: Reaches loopback through the IPv6 stack via a mapped address.

entries.label: DNS rebinding host
entries.notes: Resolves public on first lookup then to 127.0.0.1, beating check-then-fetch TOCTOU.

entries.label: Redirect to internal target
entries.notes: An allowlisted host 302-redirects to an internal target the fetcher follows.

entries.label: Userinfo @ confusion
entries.notes: Parsers that read the host as allowed.example still connect to the IP after the @.

entries.label: gopher:// Redis smuggling
entries.notes: gopher:// crafts raw TCP bytes — here a Redis command — turning SSRF into internal protocol injection.

entries.label: dict:// service probe
entries.notes: dict:// reaches line-based services such as memcached for read or interaction.

entries.label: file:// local read
entries.notes: file:// turns a URL fetcher into a local file read.

entries.label: Internal port probe
entries.notes: Vary the port to map internal services from response or timing differences.

entries.label: Out-of-band canary
entries.notes: A hit on your server confirms blind SSRF when no response is reflected in-band.
